captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: The default fallback for `POINTSTREAM_ANIMATE_ANYONE_HEIGHT` is `"512"`, but `_RuntimeConfig.height` defaults to `784`. This makes the effective default height inconsistent (and likely unintended) when the env var is not set. Change the env default to `"784"` to match the runtime config’s default behavior.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `iter_video_frames_ffmpeg()` pipes `stderr` but does not drain it until the end. If FFmpeg emits enough warnings/errors, the stderr pipe can fill and block the process, causing a hang while reading `stdout`. Consider redirecting `stderr` to `subprocess.DEVNULL`, or actively consuming `stderr` (e.g., with a background thread) while streaming frames.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `ReferenceExtractor.process()` decodes the entire video into a `frames` list, which can be very memory- and time-intensive for longer inputs (and duplicates work if only a subset of frames is needed). A more scalable approach is to stream frames and keep only the best candidate crop per track as you iterate (or do a two-pass decode: first choose best indices, then decode only those frames).

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `build_panorama_node()` is wired to accept `decoded_video_tensor` from the DAG context, but `encode_video_file()` / `encode_video_file_with_states()` never provide it in `initial_context`. As a result, `BackgroundModeler` will re-decode frames via FFmpeg even though `encode_video_file()` later decodes the video again to return `decoded_tensor`. Consider decoding once up front, passing it into the DAG via `initial_context={"chunk": chunk, "decoded_video_tensor": decoded_tensor}`, and reusing it for the return value to avoid duplicate I/O and CPU work.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `_load_original_frames()` is dead code that always raises a `RuntimeError` after doing metadata probing. This makes the class harder to maintain and can confuse future contributors. If it’s truly deprecated, consider removing it entirely, or replacing it with a private helper that’s actually used (or a clear comment at call sites if any remain).

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: This test constructs a `TaggedMultiprocessPool` but never calls `pool.shutdown()`. Even as a stub, it allocates multiprocessing queues/contexts that can leak resources and cause intermittent test warnings or hangs. Wrap the pool usage in a `try/finally` to ensure `shutdown()` is always called.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: Materializing `frames = list(iter_video_frames_ffmpeg(...))` loads the entire video into memory even though the extractor only needs up to `chunk.num_frames` and only the first confident observation per track. Consider streaming frames and stopping once you reach `frame_limit` (or once all desired player tracks have been selected), and only retaining the specific frames needed for the selected bboxes.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: Changing the process-wide working directory and mutating global environment variables inside `run_mock_pipeline()` is not thread-safe and can lead to surprising behavior if this function is reused in a long-lived process (e.g., tests running in parallel, or multiple pipeline runs in one process). Prefer avoiding `os.chdir()` entirely and pass absolute output/debug paths through to the components that need them (or wrap debug handling in a dedicated context object rather than global env).

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: Resetting the global PyTorch RNG state inside `DiffusersCompositor.process()` can introduce cross-call interference (especially under concurrency) and can affect unrelated torch code executing in the same process. Prefer using a local `torch.Generator` (and passing it into backends that support it) or isolating RNG changes via `torch.random.fork_rng()` to keep determinism without globally mutating RNG state.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: With `POINTSTREAM_ENABLE_GENAI=0`, the renderer still applies `_render_genai_baseline()` after residual composition (line 69–70), which means the output is modified even when GenAI is 'disabled'. If the intent of `POINTSTREAM_ENABLE_GENAI` is to disable the entire GenAI compositing stage, `_render_genai_baseline()` should be skipped when the flag is off (or controlled by a separate flag like `POINTSTREAM_ENABLE_GENAI_OVERLAY`).

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: For a `uint8` mask, `cv2.fillPoly` color should be an integer (e.g., `255`) rather than a float tuple `(255.0,)` to avoid implicit conversions and keep the mask logic unambiguous.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `common_quality_interval` can return an empty/inverted interval when curves don’t overlap (i.e., `high <= low`). That produces a nonsensical “common interval” that gets recorded in reports and then relies on downstream slicing to fail. Consider validating overlap here and raising (e.g., `ValueError`) when `high <= low` so callers can reliably skip the common-interval path.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `qps_for_codec()` can remap distinct VVC QPs to the same value (e.g., user input containing both 46 and 47 becomes `(46, 46)`), which then causes `encode_luma_curve()` to encode/score a duplicate QP and can trip the strict rate-monotonicity check. Consider deduping `used_qps` after remapping while preserving order.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `load_cached_clip()` is documented to return `None` when the cache record is incomplete, but it indexes several required keys (e.g., `record["video"]`, `record["video_path"]`) without guarding, so a missing/older/hand-edited `report.json` will raise `KeyError` and abort the run instead of falling back to re-extract. Consider treating missing keys as an incomplete cache record and returning `None` (e.g., via `try/except KeyError`).

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `check_bounds` treats `background_share >= 0.88` as proof that streaming "is not reaching the ledger". But the same PR's findings (§6 in `plans/BP31-findings.md`) state this bound is the wrong instrument because the share saturates and can stay high even when streaming is working. Keeping this as a hard alarm is likely to produce false positives and mislead readers; either remove the high-share alarm or soften it to a non-conclusive warning.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `src.runner.stages` now imports `src.components.background.types` at module import time. Importing any `src.components.*` submodule first executes `src/components/__init__.py`, which eagerly imports many component registries and undermines the existing intent (see `_bound_background` docstring) to keep runner imports light for config-only processes. Prefer local string constants here to avoid pulling `src.components` into every `import src.runner.stages`.

captured_inline_review_comments.author: Copilot
captured_inline_review_comments.body: `test_a_second_scene_reconstructs_rather_than_raising` does not actually exercise the runner path that used to raise (`BackgroundModelView.__post_init__` via `make_background`); it only calls `model.transmit(...)` and inspects mode strings. This can pass even if the stage regresses, so it doesn't truly guard the multi-chunk runner failure described in the class docstring. Consider driving `make_background(...)` once and calling the returned stage twice (as in `tests/runner/test_background_panorama.py::_stage_view`) to assert the second call does not raise and that `view.mode` is `full` when `artifact.mode` was `stream`.
